documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation Note
documents.content:
## Patient: Zara – Acute Cholecystitis

**HPI:** 42-year-old female presenting with acute cholecystitis, accompanied by symptomatic cholelithiasis. Reports abdominal pain localized to the right upper quadrant, radiating to the right flank.  Patient denies fever, chills, or nausea.

**Physical Exam:** Vital signs stable; abdominal examination reveals tenderness to palpation in the RUQ region. Murphy’s sign positive. No rebound tenderness.

**Management Plan:** Laparoscopic cholecystectomy performed to remove symptomatic gallbladder and bile duct obstruction. Post-operative pain management with acetaminophen and IV fluids initiated.  Patient educated on dietary restrictions and wound care instructions.  Monitor for complications such as biliary leak or infection.

diagnostics.conclusion: Right Upper Quadrant Abdominal Ultrasound abnormal findings: Acute Cholecystitis with symptomatic cholelithiasis. Key indicators: gallbladder wall thickening, cholelithiasis.
